intro: Plans from firm to tentative: from what is decided to what you only hope for, and how to say you have found something out.
p.pienso.glosa: I intend to, I plan to
p.pienso.consejo: With an infinitive it expresses intention: «pienso viajar». With «en» or «que» the meaning changes.
p.tengo previsto.consejo: It is a fairly firm plan: «tengo previsto salir el lunes». It is followed by an infinitive.
p.tengo la intención de.consejo: It sounds somewhat formal. After «de» comes an infinitive: «la intención de viajar».
p.estoy pensando en.consejo: It shows an idea not yet decided. After «en» comes an infinitive: «estoy pensando en mudarme».
p.a ver si.glosa: let's see if, I hope to
p.a ver si.consejo: It expresses hope and goes with the present: «a ver si apruebo». It is not used with the future.
p.me he enterado de que.consejo: «Enterarse» always takes «de» before the news: «me he enterado de que te vas».
p.capaz de.consejo: It works for men and women. The plural is «capaces»: the «z» becomes «c».
p.en principio.consejo: It leaves open the chance of a change: «en principio saldré el lunes».
p.si todo va bien.consejo: After «si» comes the present even if you talk about the future: «si todo va bien, saldré».
p.el máster.consejo: It is masculine and has an accent mark on the «á». The plural is «los másteres».
p.en el extranjero.consejo: It does not change: «vivir en el extranjero». An «extranjero» is also a person from another country.
p.alquilar.consejo: It works for the one who gives and the one who takes: «alquilo mi piso» and «alquilo un coche».
b1.titulo: From a firm plan to a hope
b1.texto:
With different expressions you show how certain a plan is:

- Decided plan: **voy a** + infinitive, **tengo previsto** + infinitive.
- Intention: **pienso** + infinitive, **tengo la intención de** + infinitive.
- Idea you are still considering: **estoy pensando en** + infinitive.
- Hope: **a ver si** + present.

**En principio** and **si todo va bien** leave the door open to a change.

**Enterarse de que** means to find out some news: **me he enterado de que** te vas. And **ser capaz de** + infinitive means to be able to do something; in the negative it sometimes means not daring: **no soy capaz de** decírselo.
b2.f0.texto: I've heard you're leaving your job.
b2.f1.texto: I'm planning to do a master's abroad.
b2.f2.texto: Do you know yet where you're going to study?
b2.f3.texto: I'm thinking of going to Lisbon.
b2.f4.texto: What will you do with your flat?
b2.f5.texto: I plan to rent it out.
b2.f6.texto: I wouldn't be able to go so far away.
b2.f7.texto: For now I'll leave in September if all goes well.
b4.texto:
**Pensar** changes meaning depending on what follows:

- **pensar** + infinitive: to intend. **Pienso viajar** en verano.
- **pensar en** + something: to have it in mind. **Pienso en** mi familia.
- **pensar que** + verb: to have an opinion. **Pienso que** es buena idea.

To say how firm a plan is, from most to least: **voy a**, **tengo previsto**, **pienso**, **estoy pensando en**, **a ver si**.
b4.e0.texto: I plan to travel in summer.
b4.e2.texto: Let's see if I find a flat soon.
b5.f0.texto: An open suitcase waits on Pablo's bed.
b5.f1.texto: Inside there are folded jumpers, a map of Lisbon and a grey wool scarf.
b5.f2.texto: Pablo looks at the map with half-closed eyes and traces the streets with his finger.
b5.f3.texto: Through the window comes the smell of freshly baked bread.
b5.f4.texto: He still doesn't know when he will come back to this house.
b5.f5.texto: Lucía knocks on the door with two soft taps and comes in without waiting for an answer.
b5.f6.texto: She sits on the edge of the bed and touches the scarf with her fingertips.
b5.f7.texto: Pablo tells her that he intends to rent the flat to a young couple.
b5.f8.texto: Lucía smiles slowly and looks at the suitcase with a little sadness.
b5.f9.texto: Both know that the goodbye will come with the autumn.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That's it: «a ver si» only expresses a hope.
b6.o2.refuerzo: That is a fairly firm plan.
b6.pregunta: Which of these sentences is the least certain?
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Pensar en» is to have something in mind, and it does not go with this infinitive.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Pensar que» gives an opinion and needs a conjugated verb.
b7.pregunta: You intend to study abroad. What is missing?
b8.traduccion: I plan to rent out the flat
b9.pregunta: You are still considering it. Which preposition is missing?
b10.o0.refuerzo: No: «enterarse» is not deciding, but learning some news.
b10.o1.refuerzo: That's it: «enterarse de» is receiving news.
b10.o2.refuerzo: No: it is not about a misunderstanding but about news.
b10.pregunta: Someone says «Me he enterado de que te vas». What happened?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I plan to travel.»
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Capaz para» is not used like this: you say «capaz de».
p.dejas.consejo: «Dejar el trabajo» means to quit your job. The «j» sounds like «h».
p.alquilarlo.consejo: It is «alquilar» + «lo»: the pronoun joins the infinitive. «Lo» stands for «el piso».
p.irme.consejo: It is «ir» + «me»: «irse» means to go away. The pronoun joins the infinitive.
p.septiembre.consejo: Months are not capitalised in Spanish: «septiembre». «Setiembre» is also correct.
p.encuentro.consejo: It comes from «encontrar»: the «o» becomes «ue» in «encuentro», «encuentras». After «a ver si» use the present.
p.jerséis.consejo: It is the plural of «el jersey», which ends in -y, so the plural is «jerséis», with an accent mark.
p.doblados.consejo: It comes from «doblar». It agrees with «jerséis»: masculine plural.
p.bufanda.consejo: It is feminine: «la bufanda». The plural is «las bufandas».
p.entornados.consejo: It comes from «entornar». «Ojos entornados» are eyes half-closed. It agrees with «ojos».
p.recorre.consejo: It comes from «recorrer», a regular verb. The initial «r» is strong; the one inside is «rr».
p.volverá.consejo: Future of «volver» is regular: «volver» + «á». Both «v» sound like «b».
p.golpes.consejo: It is the plural of «el golpe». «Dar golpes en la puerta» is to knock several times.
p.borde.consejo: It is masculine: «el borde». «Al borde de» means right at the edge of something.
p.intención.consejo: It is feminine: «la intención». The plural drops the accent mark: «las intenciones».
p.tristeza.consejo: It comes from «triste» + «-eza». The «z» sounds «th» in Spain. It is feminine.
p.saben.consejo: «Saber que…» introduces a fact: «saben que la despedida llegará». The «b» is soft.
p.despedida.consejo: It comes from «despedirse». It is feminine: «la despedida».
p.otoño.consejo: It is masculine: «el otoño». The «ñ» sounds like «ny». Seasons are not capitalised.
p.pensando.consejo: It is the gerund of «pensar»: «estoy pensando en…». It is formed with «-ando».
p.mudarme.consejo: It is «mudar» + «me»: «mudarse» means to move house. The pronoun joins the infinitive.
p.sabido.consejo: It is the participle of «saber», regular: «sab-» + «-ido». «He sabido» means I have found out.
p.capaz.consejo: It works for men and women. The plural is «capaces»: the final «z» becomes «c».
p.decírselo.glosa: to tell it to him or her
p.decírselo.consejo: It is «decir» + «se» + «lo»: «se» replaces «le» before «lo». The accent mark is kept.
